items.title: Ketamine assisted psychotherapy to reduce chronic neuropathic pain: A mixed-methods randomized pilot trial.
items.summary_en: Randomized pilot trial (n=30, 87% follow-up) comparing ketamine infusions, psychotherapy, or combined treatment for chronic neuropathic pain. Ketamine: three IV infusions over 16 weeks; psychotherapy: 16 weekly CBT and mindfulness sessions. Primary outcome was feasibility; exploratory outcomes included pain interference and intensity. Most feasibility criteria met; clinically meaningful pain reductions observed across groups. Study design and safety data support further efficacy trials.

items.title: A contemporary exploration of motivations and practices of psychedelic use among emerging adult cannabis users in the United States: A qualitative analysis.
items.summary_en: Qualitative study (2022-2023) examining motivations for psalmoterapeutic use among ethnically diverse cannabis-using emerging adults in the US. Thematic analysis identified four key domains: social/contextual factors, user expectancies, motives (spiritual exploration, social connection, self-treatment), and practices (microdosing, intentional use). Findings contribute to understanding contemporary psychedelic use patterns.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Psychedelic Microdosing on Psychological Outcomes in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.summary_en: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies (3,681 participants) examining psychedelic microdosing in healthy adults. RCTs of psilocybin and LSD showed subjective and neurophysiological effects but minimal impact on cognition, creativity, or sustained mood improvement. Observational studies reported mood and personality benefits, suggesting study design influences outcomes. Safety data from RCTs indicate generally minor adverse effects.
items.notable_reason: Large meta-analysis (n=3,681 participants across 24 studies, 6 contributing to pooled analyses) synthesizing RCT and observational evidence on psilocybin and LSD microdosing with safety outcomes.

items.title: Psychoactive and Neurobiological Effects of Ketamine in Humans: A Scoping Review of Clinical Evidence.
items.summary_en: A scoping review examining clinical evidence on ketamine's psychoactive and neurobiological effects in humans. The study synthesizes research on ketamine's mechanisms of action, psychological impacts, and neural effects across clinical populations, providing a comprehensive overview of current knowledge in this therapeutic research area.

items.title: Ketamine preserves perineuronal nets in chronic stressed mice brain through the inhibition of microglia activation.
items.summary_en: Mouse study examining ketamine's antidepressant mechanisms in chronic stress. Ketamine preserved perineuronal nets (PNNs)—extracellular structures regulating synaptic plasticity—in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex by inhibiting microglial activation. Treatment reversed stress-induced PNN degradation and depression-like behavior, suggesting microglia suppression as a therapeutic target.

items.title: Psilocybin-containing mushroom-assisted psychotherapy is associated with sustained psychological and somatic improvements: two case studies from Jamaica.
items.summary_en: Two case studies from Jamaica examined psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy using the De La Haye Protocol, combining micro-doses (1-2 mg) and high-doses (40-60 mg) with psychotherapy. Both patients showed sustained improvements: reduced anxiety and pain in case 1, and enhanced mood with recovery of smell/taste in case 2. High mystical experience scores were recorded at two-month follow-up.

items.title: Investigating the effects of chlorogenic acid on novel object recognition memory impairment, hyperlocomotion, and prefrontal BDNF expression in a sub-chronic ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like rat model.
items.summary_en: Rat study (both sexes) examined chlorogenic acid's effects on ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like symptoms. Sub-chronic ketamine (7 days, 30 mg/kg) impaired novel object recognition and increased locomotion in both sexes, with sex-specific effects on grooming and rearing. Single chlorogenic acid dose (150 mg/kg) partially reversed some behavioral changes and partially restored prefrontal BDNF expression decreased by ketamine.

items.title: Well-being as a primary endpoint in clinical trials: a call for consensus.
items.summary_en: Psychiatric trials typically measure success through symptom reduction, but patients prioritize meaning, vitality, and functioning. Psychedelic trials demonstrate this gap: significant well-being improvements often occur despite modest symptom effects. Researchers propose elevating well-being to co-primary endpoint status in clinical trials, with a validated consensus instrument and safeguards ensuring therapies don't worsen underlying conditions.

items.title: Psychedelics and astrocytes: a hypothesis-driven perspective on neuro-glial integration, network plasticity, and neuroimmune reprogramming.
items.summary_en: This hypothesis-driven review examines astrocytes' potential role in psychedelic-induced brain changes. While serotonin 2A receptor signaling on neurons remains central, evidence suggests astrocytes—traditionally viewed as passive support cells—actively integrate neuromodulatory signals and coordinate synaptic plasticity, metabolic coupling, and immune responses. The authors propose a neuro-glial ensemble framework where neuron-astrocyte interactions constitute functional units underlying psychedelic-induced network reorganization and therapeutic effects across neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: Smooth Sailing: Definium’s LSD Voyage Hits Primary and Key Secondary Endpoints in GAD
items.summary_en: Definium Therapeutics announced positive Phase 3 trial results for LSD (DT120) in generalised anxiety disorder, meeting primary and key secondary endpoints. This follows successful Phase 3 results in major depressive disorder announced two months earlier, marking significant progress in clinical development of lysergamides for psychiatric conditions.
items.notable_reason: Phase 3 RCT results meeting primary and key secondary endpoints in GAD, following recent positive Phase 3 results in MDD for the same compound.

items.title: Two Years After Rejection, Resilient Quietly Refiles MDMA for PTSD Application
items.summary_en: Resilient Therapeutics has resubmitted its MDMA application for PTSD treatment to regulatory authorities, two years after an initial rejection. The company's resubmission follows previous clinical data evaluations.

items.title: Effects of naturalistic psychedelic use on executive functioning: An online survey of lifetime history and recent use in university students.
items.summary_en: Cross-sectional online study of 1342 university students examining executive functioning in relation to psychedelic use. Participants completed the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task and reported lifetime/recent psychedelic use. Lifetime (n=224) and recent (n=114) users showed better performance on most measures: fewer errors, more correct responses, and more categories achieved. Moderate-dose users completed more categories than low-dose users. Results suggest naturalistic psychedelic use associates with enhanced executive functioning.

items.title: Psilocybin-associated microRNA changes in the pig brain: Establishing an nCounter pipeline for cross-species microRNA quantification.
items.summary_en: Study in adolescent female pigs examined microRNA expression changes in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus after single psilocybin dose. Using NanoString nCounter analysis, researchers identified 12 dysregulated microRNAs in prefrontal cortex and 2-4 in hippocampus at day 1 and day 7 post-administration. Nine of 18 identified microRNAs previously linked to depression. Findings demonstrate region- and time-dependent microRNA changes, establishing a validated pipeline for cross-species psychedelic neurochemistry research.

items.title: Real-World Psilocybin Therapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Retrospective Observational Study.
items.summary_en: Retrospective analysis of 19 treatment-resistant depression patients at Zurich Psychiatric University Hospital receiving psilocybin therapy (20-35 mg, 1-4 sessions). MADRS scores decreased significantly (30.78 to 19.89, Hedges' g=1.37), with 33% response and 22% remission rates. BDI scores also improved (32.33 to 23.28, g=0.77). No serious adverse events documented. This real-world evidence demonstrates psilocybin's clinical feasibility and safety outside controlled trials.

items.title: Mechanisms of Action and Change in Psychedelic-Assisted Therapies: A Holistic Framework for Ethical, Competent Clinical Care.
items.summary_en: This review presents a multilevel framework for understanding psychedelic-assisted therapies (PATs) for trauma and stress-related disorders. Rather than focusing solely on neurobiological mechanisms, the authors integrate neuroplasticity, memory updating, relational dynamics, and meaning-making as interacting factors in therapeutic change. The paper emphasizes how preparation, altered states, and integration create windows for experiential relearning, while discussing ethical considerations and clinical guidance for practitioners.

items.title: Combined Ketamine and Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy: Leveraging Metaplasticity to Enhance Treatment Outcomes.
items.summary_en: Recent research examines combining ketamine with cognitive-behavioral therapy to treat depression, particularly in treatment-resistant cases. The approach leverages metaplasticity—the brain's capacity to modify its own plasticity—potentially enhancing therapeutic outcomes through synergistic effects of rapid-acting ketamine and behavioral interventions.

items.title: Synergistic and Scalable: A Review of Integrated Digital and Biological Interventions.
items.summary_en: This review examines how digital therapeutics (internet-based therapy, cognitive training) combined with neuroplasticity-enhancing biological treatments—including psychedelics—may synergistically improve psychiatric outcomes. Evidence suggests pairing approaches can enhance efficacy of both components. The authors discuss clinical applications, regulatory considerations, and the need for rigorous randomized trials and real-world effectiveness studies.

items.title: Sex-sensitive serotonergic signaling in psychedelic pharmacology.
items.summary_en: Classic serotonergic psychedelics primarily act via 5-HT2A receptor agonism, yet show heterogeneous therapeutic effects. This review synthesizes evidence that biological sex and endocrine state modulate key serotonergic mechanisms—including 5-HT1A feedback, 5-HT2A signaling, and neuroplasticity—relevant to psychedelic action. Most clinical and preclinical studies lack sex-by-treatment designs. The authors prioritize sex-informed translational research to better understand variability in psychedelic responses.

items.title: Intravenous Ketamine reduces psychological pain in suicidal inpatients: A secondary analysis of a six-week randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.summary_en: Secondary analysis of the KETIS trial (n=156 suicidal inpatients) examined intravenous ketamine's effect on psychological pain. Two 40-min infusions (0.5 mg/kg) or placebo, 24h apart, were given alongside standard care. Psychological pain decreased significantly more with ketamine within 96h (p<0.001), with largest effects at 40min-24h, but differences disappeared by week 2-6. Effects remained after adjusting for depression and hopelessness.
items.notable_reason: Secondary analysis of a 6-week double-blind RCT (n=156) examining ketamine's mechanism of action on psychological pain in suicidal inpatients—a novel treatment target with rapid-onset effects.

items.title: Discordant signals: How outcome measurement shapes interpretation of ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Secondary analysis of 71 treatment-resistant depression patients examined ketamine response using three rating scales (MADRS, BDI-II, CGI-S). Change scores showed variable correlations across instruments (ρ = 0.13–0.69). MADRS detected greater symptom reduction (54.2%) than BDI-II (41.9%), with larger effect sizes (d = 1.78 vs 1.34). Suicidality improved on both measures. Results demonstrate that outcome measurement choice significantly influences effect size estimates and perceived treatment response magnitude.

items.title: Psychedelics in psychiatry: from promise to translation.
items.summary_en: A review examining psychedelics' therapeutic potential in psychiatry finds that clinical translation remains premature. The authors argue that progress requires simultaneous advances in mechanistic research, clinical implementation, regulatory frameworks, and public discourse.

items.title: 'So many relationships in the room': Participant perspectives on the affordances and challenges of co-therapy in psychedelic assisted therapy.
items.summary_en: Qualitative study of 18 participants from a phase 2 randomized trial examining experiences of co-therapy (two therapists) in psilocybin-assisted therapy for generalized anxiety disorder. Semi-structured interviews (n=29) before and after dosing sessions revealed three themes: co-therapy provided safety and trust; influenced therapeutic processes; and shaped credibility of insights. Co-therapy functioned as both a safety measure and therapeutic enhancer, though accessibility considerations remain.

items.title: Adjunctive transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation following loss of response to maintenance intranasal esketamine in treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Case report examining adjunctive transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in a patient with treatment-resistant depression who lost response to maintenance intranasal esketamine. The study explores combining two neuromodulation approaches when initial ketamine treatment efficacy wanes.

items.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy for treatment-resistant major depressive disorder in a public healthcare setting: a randomized controlled trial.
items.summary_en: Randomized controlled trial (n=60) examining single-dose psilocybin (25 mg) with psychological support for treatment-resistant depression in NHS setting. At week 3, psilocybin showed significantly greater symptom reduction (MADRS: -10.41, Cohen's d=-1.70) versus placebo, sustained at week 6. High retention (59/60 completed follow-up). Results support confirmatory trials.
items.notable_reason: Randomized controlled trial in public healthcare setting (NHS) demonstrating significant efficacy (Cohen's d = -1.70) for psilocybin in treatment-resistant major depressive disorder with high completion rates (59/60 participants).

items.title: Feasibility and Tolerability of Psilocybin for Phantom Limb Pain.
items.summary_en: Pilot randomized controlled trial (n=9) examined psilocybin feasibility and safety for phantom limb pain. Participants received 25 mg psilocybin (n=5) or niacin placebo (n=4) with preparatory and integration sessions. No serious adverse events or suicidality emerged. Transient anxiety, discomfort, and BP/HR elevations resolved before discharge. Two weeks post-administration, pain ratings showed trends toward >30% reduction, suggesting preliminary feasibility for further investigation.

items.title: Microdosing psychedelics: What, why, when, and how often? Insights from an international survey of people who use psychedelics.
items.summary_en: GPS 2025, an international survey of 5,399 microdosers, examined patterns of use across 19 languages. Psilocybin dominated (81.1%), followed by LSD (39.6%). The Fadiman protocol (one day on, two days off) was most common among regular users (24.3%). Participants typically microdosed in nature (58.9%), with introspective focus (56.8%) or leisure activities (43%), supporting set and setting integration.
items.notable_reason: Large cross-sectional study (n=5399 microdosers) across 19 languages examining global patterns of psychedelic microdosing with detailed behavioral data.

items.title: Impact of Psilocybin on Motor Function in Healthy Participants: A Phase 1, Randomised, Triple-Blind, Dose-Finding Study.
items.summary_en: Phase 1 randomised triple-blind study examining psilocybin's effects on motor function in healthy adults. Participants received doses of 5–20 mg psilocybin with motor assessments at 1.5–4.5 hours post-dose. Feasibility and safety were primary endpoints; exploratory outcomes included grip strength, dexterity, reaction time and upper limb function. Results provide evidence for safe administration of movement tasks during psilocybin effects.

items.title: The occurrence and potential role of mystical experiences in MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD: A secondary analysis.
items.summary_en: Secondary analysis of two phase 2 randomized trials examined mystical experiences during MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) for chronic PTSD. Fifty-three participants received MDMA or active placebo with psychotherapy; mystical experiences were measured using MEQ30 after each session. MDMA produced significantly higher mystical experience scores than placebo. Positive mood components, rather than full mystical states, most strongly associated with PTSD symptom reduction. Results warrant cautious interpretation due to limited sample size.

items.title: A suite of engineered mice for interrogating psychedelic drug actions.
items.summary_en: Researchers developed engineered mouse models to study how classical psychedelics like LSD and psilocybin work in the brain. These substances show therapeutic promise for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and headache disorders by activating the 5-HT2A receptor. The new transgenic mice will help clarify this receptor's specific role in psychedelic effects.

items.title: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #229: SAMHSA Convenes Experts; AtaiBeckley’s Road to Lilly; Turnbull Doubles Down on BOL-148; Compass Talks Indication Expansion, Could VA Help?
items.summary_en: SAMHSA convened experts in Washington D.C. for a two-day consultation on data gaps in monitoring psychedelic use and misuse in the U.S. Participants included federal agencies, researchers, regulators, and industry representatives. The meeting addressed evidence collection needs as clinical development of psychedelics-assisted therapies advances.

items.title: Prevalence of Potential Contraindications and Risk Factors Relevant to MDMA-Assisted Therapy Among U.S. Veterans with Posttraumatic Stress Disorder.
items.summary_en: National cross-sectional study (2018-2023) of 303,000-326,000 U.S. veterans with PTSD examined eligibility for MDMA-assisted therapy. Findings: 15-17% had absolute contraindications, 55-58% had conditional/modifiable risk factors, and 86-88% took medications with potential MDMA interactions. While many veterans require additional evaluation, careful management of modifiable conditions may enable treatment access.

items.title: Blinding Integrity and Psychedelic Drug Trials.
items.summary_en: This article examines blinding integrity in psychedelic clinical trials, addressing methodological challenges in maintaining participant and researcher blindness when testing substances with distinctive subjective effects.

items.title: Blinding Integrity and Psychedelic Drug Trials-Reply.
items.summary_en: This is a reply article addressing blinding integrity in psychedelic research trials. Without access to the full text, the specific methodological concerns and responses cannot be detailed. The piece likely discusses challenges in maintaining double-blind conditions in clinical studies of hallucinogens, given their distinctive subjective effects.

items.title: Blinding Integrity and Psychedelic Drug Trials.
items.summary_en: This article examines blinding integrity in psychedelic clinical trials. Effective blinding is challenging in psychedelic research due to participants' perceptual experiences. The study discusses methodological implications for maintaining trial validity and suggests strategies to strengthen blinding procedures in future psychedelic investigations.

items.title: Psychedelics and women's mental health: the effects of female sex hormones on psychedelics' efficacy and tolerability.
items.summary_en: Narrative review examining how female sex hormones (estradiol and progesterone) modulate psychedelic pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and brain networks. Evidence suggests hormones alter gastrointestinal physiology, hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4, CYP2D6), and serotonergic signaling including 5-HT2A receptor density across menstrual cycles. Despite preclinical and neuroimaging data, direct human pharmacokinetic studies in psychedelic-assisted therapies remain absent, highlighting a critical gap given women's higher burden of mood and stress disorders.

items.title: A crucial cautionary note on frequently incorrect dose equivalence between ketamine and esketamine.
items.summary_en: Researchers warn of frequent errors in dose equivalence calculations between ketamine and esketamine. The article highlights critical discrepancies in clinical dosing practices that could affect treatment outcomes and patient safety in psychedelic-assisted therapies.

items.title: Safety and Efficacy of Psilocybin During Anticancer Treatment: A Phase II Trial Secondary Analysis.
items.summary_en: Phase II secondary analysis (n=30) examined psilocybin-assisted therapy safety and efficacy in cancer patients with depression, comparing those receiving concurrent systemic treatment (n=17) versus not (n=13). Both groups showed significant MADRS score improvements at weeks 1, 3, and 8 with no significant differences. Adverse events were frequent but comparable; severe events occurred only in the treated group but were deemed unrelated to psilocybin.

items.title: Psychological change processes in alcohol use disorder: A qualitative study of 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (5-MeO-DMT) with cognitive behavioural therapy.
items.summary_en: Qualitative study embedded in a phase 2a open-label trial examining psychological change processes in 10 participants with moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder receiving a single intranasal dose of 5-MeO-DMT alongside cognitive behavioural therapy for relapse prevention. Semi-structured interviews with participants and therapists at day 1 and week 12 explored acute experiences, perceived psychological and behavioural changes, and the perceived role of therapeutic support.
items.notable_reason: First-in-human clinical trial of intranasal 5-MeO-DMT (novel route of administration) for alcohol use disorder with integrated qualitative analysis of change mechanisms.

items.title: Psilocybin for Fear of Cancer Recurrence.
items.summary_en: Study examining psilocybin's potential therapeutic effects on fear of cancer recurrence in cancer survivors. Research explores how hallucinogenic substances may reduce anxiety related to disease progression concerns in this patient population.

items.title: Cardiovascular safety of psilocybin in psychiatric practice: a narrative review.
items.summary_en: A narrative review of psilocybin's cardiovascular safety as psychiatric applications expand beyond clinical trials. Analysis of hemodynamics, QT interval effects, and serotonin receptor interactions shows mean systolic/diastolic increases (~19/8.7 mmHg) peaking 60-90 min post-dose in supervised settings. Serious acute events remain rare in screened participants, but risk assessment must account for comorbidities, drug interactions, and repeated exposure.

items.title: Barriers and Facilitators for Psychedelic Research and Regulation in Brazil: Insights From Diverse Stakeholders.
items.summary_en: Qualitative interview study (n=26) examining barriers, facilitators, and stakeholder perspectives on psychedelic research and regulation in Brazil. Diverse participants included Indigenous leaders, clinicians, policymakers, and activists. Thematic analysis identified four barriers (accessibility, regulation, limited knowledge, risks), three facilitators (innovation need, scientific advancement, legal loopholes), and four perspectives (ancestral knowledge integration, scientific rigor, user autonomy, social benefits).

items.title: Ketamine and Evolving Neuroplasticity.
items.summary_en: This review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence on ketamine's time-dependent neuroplastic effects in treating mood disorders. Unlike traditional antidepressants, ketamine acts via NMDA receptor antagonism, triggering glutamatergic signaling that promotes synaptic plasticity and rapid symptom relief. The review examines molecular changes including BDNF signaling, mTOR pathway activation, and AMPA receptor modulation, and correlates these with clinical outcomes in mood, cognition, and functioning.

items.title: AMPA receptor modulation in depression: from molecular mechanisms of plasticity to therapeutic translation.
items.summary_en: AMPA receptor modulators, particularly AMPAkines, show promise for rapid-acting depression treatment. These positive allosteric modulators enhance glutamatergic signaling and BDNF expression. Preclinical studies demonstrate antidepressant effects with low-impact compounds offering favorable safety profiles, though seizure risk exists with high-impact variants. Limited clinical trials support efficacy, but translational challenges remain: narrow therapeutic windows, suboptimal pharmacokinetics, and weak animal model predictivity.

items.summary_en: Dreaming during anaesthesia: a scoping review.

items.title: Letter to the Editor: Esketamine in treatment-resistant depression: Beyond symptom reduction toward psychopathological network reorganization.
items.summary_en: Letter examining esketamine's mechanism in treatment-resistant depression, proposing that therapeutic effects may extend beyond symptom reduction to involve reorganization of psychopathological networks. The analysis suggests esketamine's action operates at a systems level rather than simply alleviating individual symptoms.

items.title: Mystery shopper assessments of cannabis retailer practices and regulatory compliance in five U.S. states, 2025.
items.summary_en: Mystery shopper assessments of cannabis retailer practices and regulatory compliance in five U.S. states, 2025.

items.title: A systematic review of the pharmacokinetics of classical serotonergic psychedelic compounds in healthy adult subjects.
items.summary_en: A systematic review of 32 trials examined pharmacokinetic profiles of classical serotonergic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline, 5-MeO-DMT) in healthy adults. LSD was most studied, followed by DMT via intravenous and oral routes, and psilocybin. Mescaline had limited data (2 trials). Key findings reveal dose-proportional responses and important variations in absorption, distribution, and elimination between compounds with implications for clinical and research applications.
items.notable_reason: Systematic review synthesizing pharmacokinetic data across 32 trials of multiple classical psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline, 5-MEO-DMT) with implications for clinical and research design.

items.title: The Serotonin 2B (5-HT2B) Receptor: A Narrative Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence on the Safety Considerations and Therapeutic Potential for the Treatment of Depression.
items.summary_en: Narrative review examining 5-HT2B receptor's role in depression treatment. While peripheral 5-HT2B agonism risks valvular heart disease (documented with fenfluramine, ergot agonists), central mechanisms show antidepressant potential through astrocytic and neuronal signaling. Classical psychedelics bind 5-HT2B receptors; cumulative exposure risks from intermittent dosing remain understudied. Some approved antidepressant adjuncts target this pathway, warranting further clinical investigation of safety-efficacy profiles.

items.title: Treatment-emergent psychiatric adverse events in patient-reported outcomes during ketamine use for major depressive disorder: a retrospective analysis.
items.summary_en: Retrospective analysis of 28 inpatients with treatment-resistant depression receiving 8 ketamine infusions as add-on therapy. Psychiatric adverse events were tracked using IDS-SR-30. Sleep disturbances were the most common emerging symptom, with nighttime sleep problems and early waking persisting through follow-up. Appetite and weight changes occurred early in treatment. Mood, cognitive symptoms, and suicidal ideation remained rare, suggesting ketamine's psychiatric safety profile in this population.

items.title: Regulatory context for protocol amendments and public reporting in psychedelic trials.
items.summary_en: This article examines regulatory frameworks governing protocol amendments and public reporting in clinical trials of hallucinogens. The study addresses compliance requirements and transparency standards for researchers conducting psychedelic research, emphasizing the importance of proper documentation and disclosure practices in this evolving field.

items.title: Brain iron-sensitive markers (magnetic susceptibility and R2*) predict antidepressant response to ketamine in treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Double-blind RCT with open-label extension examining repeated IV ketamine in 17 Japanese TRD patients. Baseline brain iron levels (measured via QSM and R2* mapping) predicted antidepressant response. Higher iron in right nucleus accumbens and left amygdala correlated with greater improvement in retardation and vegetative symptoms on MADRS, suggesting iron-related dopamine dysfunction may indicate ketamine treatment response.

items.title: 5-HT
items.summary_en: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study (n=12) examined how pindolol pretreatment affects subjective responses to DMT. Participants received sub-hallucinogenic intravenous DMT (0.1 mg/kg) after oral pindolol (30 mg). Pindolol pretreatment significantly increased DMT-induced subjective effects via 5-HT2A receptor mechanisms, with moderate effect size. Results suggest serotonergic pathways mediate subjective experiences potentially relevant to therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Intranasal Ketamine for Existential Distress in Advanced Cancer.
items.summary_en: The INKeD-PC trial evaluated intranasal ketamine for depression and existential distress in 15 advanced cancer patients receiving palliative care. Participants received 3 ketamine doses. Secondary outcome analysis showed significant improvements across all measures: anxiety (d=1.22), death anxiety (d=0.91), symptom burden (d=1.21), and quality of life (d=1.53), exceeding clinically meaningful thresholds. Qualitative feedback supported quantitative findings.

items.title: Faster and greater antidepressant response to intravenous ketamine in bipolar compared with unipolar treatment-resistant depression: Diagnostic and sex-related findings from a naturalistic study.
items.summary_en: Observational study (N=97) comparing intravenous ketamine efficacy in treatment-resistant unipolar versus bipolar depression. Both groups showed significant symptom reduction over three months, but bipolar patients demonstrated faster and greater improvement from week 2 onwards on MADRS and CGI-S scales. Dissociative effects were measured with CADSS. Real-world data suggest diagnostic differences in ketamine response.

items.title: Efficacy of N, N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) psychedelic therapy for substance misuse: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary_en: Systematic review and meta-analysis (1960-2024) of DMT intervention studies across multiple databases examined its efficacy for substance misuse. DMT showed large overall effect sizes for substance abuse reduction, with enhanced outcomes when combined with psychotherapy. However, included studies had substantial methodological limitations and high bias risk. Results are preliminary and highly heterogeneous across substance types and study designs, warranting cautious interpretation pending future rigorous research.

items.title: Subjective and neurocognitive profiling of clinical doses of 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) in healthy volunteers: implications for therapeutic use.
items.summary_en: Subjective and neurocognitive profiling of clinical doses of 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) in healthy volunteers: implications for therapeutic use.

items.title: Adenosine surges: A step forward in understanding antidepressant actions of ketamine.
items.summary_en: Recent research investigates adenosine signaling as a mechanism underlying ketamine's antidepressant effects. The study advances understanding of how this dissociative anesthetic produces rapid mood improvement, identifying adenosine surges as a potential key pathway. These findings may inform development of novel antidepressant treatments targeting similar neurochemical processes.

items.title: Role of concomitant benzodiazepines, lithium, and lamotrigine in modulating the antidepressant effects of subcutaneous esketamine in patients with treatment-resistant depressive episodes: A retrospective naturalistic study.
items.summary_en: Retrospective study of 178 patients examined how benzodiazepines, lithium, and lamotrigine affect esketamine treatment outcomes in treatment-resistant depression. Weekly subcutaneous esketamine (0.5-1.0 mg/kg) for 6 weeks significantly reduced depression scores. Concomitant benzodiazepine use was associated with higher depression scores, while lithium and lamotrigine showed no significant interaction effects.

items.title: Standardized chronic restraint stress protocols reveal dynamic evolution of behavioral adaptations in male mice: implications for translational neuroscience.
items.summary_en: Longitudinal study in male mice comparing chronic restraint stress (CRS) protocols to model stress-induced behavioral adaptations. Short intense CRS (6h/day, 3 days) induced persistent avoidance and repetitive behaviors, while prolonged CRS (2h/day, 10-14 days) progressively impaired reward-seeking and coping. A 10-day protocol emerged as critical threshold for comorbid avoidance and reward-processing deficits. Ketamine reversed reward-seeking impairment; paroxetine alleviated both avoidance and reward-seeking deficits.

items.title: The role of therapeutic alliance in psilocybin treatment for treatment-resistant depression: A post hoc path analysis.
items.summary_en: Post hoc path analysis (N=79) examined therapeutic alliance's role in psilocybin treatment for treatment-resistant depression. While pre-dosing alliance showed weak correlation with depression improvement (MADRS Week 3), psychedelic experience measures correlated more strongly. Alliance had minimal direct effect on outcomes but significantly influenced the intensity of psychedelic experiences, which independently predicted clinical improvement.

items.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder: Perspective from meta-analysis.
items.summary_en: Meta-analysis of six randomized controlled trials examined psilocybin-assisted therapy for major depressive disorder. Standard-dose psilocybin (25 mg) showed superior efficacy compared to placebo and control conditions in reducing depressive symptoms (SMD: -1.05, p=0.0002). Low-dose psilocybin showed less consistent effects. Results suggest psilocybin may be a promising treatment option, though methodological variation across studies warrants further investigation.
items.notable_reason: Meta-analysis across six RCTs synthesizing efficacy and safety data for psilocybin in MDD with quantified effect sizes (SMD −1.05), addressing a major clinical indication.

items.title: Detecting neuroplastic effects induced by ketamine in healthy human subjects: A multimodal approach.
items.summary_en: A multimodal PET/MRI study examined neuroplastic changes following a single intravenous ketamine dose (1 mg/kg) in 11 healthy male participants. Brain scans were conducted before and 1-8 days post-administration to assess structural and functional alterations induced by this psychedelic compound.

items.title: A phase 2 uncontrolled, open-label study of intranasal BPL-003 (5-methoxy-
items.summary_en: Phase 2a open-label trial of intranasal BPL-003 (5-methoxy-DMT) in 12 treatment-resistant depression patients. Single 10 mg dose showed rapid symptom improvement: mean MADRS score reduction of 12.2-13.0 points sustained over 12 weeks, with 83% responders and 64% reaching remission. Safety profile acceptable; mild-to-moderate adverse events predominant (nausea, nasal discomfort), one severe hypertension episode resolved within observation period. Results warrant further controlled investigation.

items.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of esketamine versus injectable racemic ketamine and oral antidepressants for major depressive disorder: A population-based target trial emulation.
items.summary_en: Population-based study (2018-2024) comparing esketamine, injectable ketamine, and oral antidepressants for major depressive disorder in 4505, 197694, and 887220 patients respectively. Using propensity score matching and Cox regression: esketamine vs injectable ketamine showed higher risks of suicidal ideation (HR=1.24), anxiety (HR=1.55), insomnia (HR=1.25), and cardiac arrest (HR=1.57). Esketamine vs oral antidepressants showed lower suicide risk.
items.notable_reason: Large observational study (n=1,089,419 total) with real-world comparative safety data on esketamine vs. injectable ketamine, addressing clinical outcomes including suicidality and cardiac safety.

items.title: Bifunctional Modulation of NMDA and Opioid Receptors in Ketamine Reinforcement and Misuse: Implications for Substance Use Disorder Treatment.
items.summary_en: Review examining ketamine's neurochemical mechanisms in reinforcement and misuse potential. Study highlights bifunctional modulation of NMDA and opioid receptors in addiction-relevant brain circuits, with (S)-ketamine enantiomer identified as primary misuse risk driver. Discusses implications for balancing therapeutic benefits in depression and substance use disorder treatment against recreational appeal and misuse concerns in clinical settings.

items.title: Ayahuasca-inspired DMT/harmine formulation alters creative thinking dynamics during artistic creation.
items.summary_en: A double-blind, placebo-controlled study (n=30) examined how DMT/harmine and harmine alone affected creative thinking using convergent/divergent thinking tasks and real-world painting assessments. DMT/harmine impaired convergent thinking, especially in high-reasoning individuals, while divergent thinking showed trend-level reductions. Both compounds reduced incubation-related process transitions, with DMT/harmine specifically decreasing transitions to creative insight. Subjective experiences predicted divergent thinking outcomes.

items.title: Psychedelic and Medicinal Mushrooms: Potent Source of Active Metabolites and Medicines
items.summary_en: Review of medicinal mushrooms and their bioactive compounds. Analysis of English-language publications examined various mushroom species and their biological properties, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, anticancer, and antimicrobial effects. Active metabolites in mycelium and fruiting bodies account for these properties, with distribution and effects varying by mushroom type and compound chemistry.

items.title: A cross-national comparison of nonmedical and medical use of psychedelic drugs in the international cannabis policy study
items.summary_en: Cross-sectional survey across Canada, US, Australia, and New Zealand (2023 ICPS) found 19% lifetime use of psilocybin, LSD, MDMA, or ketamine. Psilocybin was most common (16.3% in Canada, 13.0% USA, 12.1% New Zealand, 7.8% Australia). Only 10-20% of users discussed medical use with healthcare providers; over one-third of past-year users reported doing so.
items.notable_reason: Large cross-national observational study (n appears substantial across 4 countries) examining prevalence and medical engagement with psilocybin, LSD, MDMA, and ketamine in the context of renewed therapeutic interest.

items.title: Last resort: the ethical obligation to offer ketamine in psychiatric euthanasia and assisted suicide.
items.summary_en: A study argues that in countries permitting psychiatric euthanasia/assisted suicide, ketamine—shown to rapidly reduce suicidality and depression—should be offered as a last-resort treatment before approval. IV ketamine and intranasal esketamine may clarify decision-making capacity and determine treatability. Patients refusing ketamine should undergo formal review processes protecting their right to die while preventing avoidable deaths.

items.title: Convergent neuroimmune signaling underlying rapid antidepressant response to ketamine and psychedelics.
items.summary_en: Study integrating CSF proteomics, iPSC transcriptomics, and clinical data (n=16-39 TRD patients) identifies convergent neuroimmune mechanisms underlying rapid antidepressant effects of ketamine and serotonergic psychedelics. Despite distinct receptor targets, both compound classes modulate conserved immune pathways, with IL-15 and MCP-1 as key regulatory hubs. Ketamine responders showed baseline IL-15 reduction and elevated B-cell signaling, reversed post-treatment.
items.notable_reason: First study integrating CSF proteomics, iPSC transcriptomics, MEG, and plasma biomarkers across ketamine and psychedelics to identify convergent neuroimmune mechanisms of rapid antidepressant action.

items.title: Dimensional effect profiles in treatment-resistant depression: A naturalistic, prospective head-to-head comparison of arTMS, esketamine nasal spray, and oral brexpiprazole.
items.summary_en: Naturalistic study comparing three treatments for treatment-resistant depression (TRD): esketamine nasal spray, accelerated repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (arTMS), and brexpiprazole augmentation. In 101 participants assessed at baseline and one month, all treatments reduced depression severity and anhedonia. Brexpiprazole showed greater rumination improvement, esketamine enhanced affective and cognitive symptoms, while esketamine and arTMS both reduced anxiety. Results suggest domain-specific treatment profiles in routine clinical settings.

items.title: Feasibility, safety and preliminary effects of ibogaine in patients with moderate and severe alcohol use disorder: a pilot, open-label study.
items.summary_en: Feasibility, safety and preliminary effects of ibogaine in patients with moderate and severe alcohol use disorder: a pilot, open-label study.

items.title: Candidate Biomarkers of Bipolar Disorder Progression: Implications for Ketamine and Psychedelic Interventions.
items.summary_en: A narrative review examined biomarkers of bipolar disorder (BD) progression and ketamine/psychedelic interventions. Literature search across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified associations between advanced BD and inflammatory, neurotrophic, neuroimaging, and epigenetic abnormalities. However, findings were heterogeneous with modest effect sizes, often cross-sectional, and many biomarkers reflected current mood state rather than cumulative progression. BDNF and inflammatory markers showed limited specificity.

items.title: Hepatic Safety of Ketamine and Esketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Real-World Cohort Study.
items.summary_en: Real-world cohort study (n=51) examining hepatic safety of ketamine and esketamine for treatment-resistant depression at Mayo Clinic (2017–2024). No clinically meaningful changes in liver enzyme trajectories were observed. Three patients (5.9%) showed elevations ≥2× upper limit of normal, all attributed to alcohol use, myalgias, or pre-existing steatosis rather than dissociatives. Subanesthetic doses appear hepatically safe.

items.title: Esketamine in Treatment-Resistant Depression: Clinical and Translational Perspectives.
items.summary_en: Intranasal esketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist, shows rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression by enhancing glutamatergic signaling and synaptic plasticity. Randomized controlled trials demonstrate symptom improvement within hours, though effects on suicidality varied. Common side effects—dissociation, dizziness, elevated blood pressure—are typically transient.

items.title: Adjunctive Pharmacotherapy for Major Depressive Disorder with Anxiety Symptoms: from Monoamines to Recent Clinical Evidence.
items.summary_en: Adjunctive Pharmacotherapy for Major Depressive Disorder with Anxiety Symptoms: from Monoamines to Recent Clinical Evidence.

items.title: Systems-based psychiatry: insights from psychedelic research on mechanisms of healing.
items.summary_en: Systems-based psychiatry: insights from psychedelic research on mechanisms of healing.

items.title: [Illicit use of classic psychedelics and suicidality: A systematic literature review].
items.summary_en: Systematic review of PubMed and Scopus (March 2026) examining illicit use of classic psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, DMT, mescaline) and suicidality outcomes. Study followed PRISMA criteria to synthesize conflicting literature on effects of these substances on suicidal ideation, planning, attempts, and completed suicides. Review aims to clarify relationship between illicit psychedelic use and suicide risk.
items.notable_reason: Systematic review (PRISMA-compliant) addressing a critical clinical safety question (suicidality) across multiple classic psychedelics with broad database coverage.

items.title: CB1R-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis may contribute to the antidepressant effects of esketamine in a chronic variable stress male mouse model.
items.summary_en: A mouse study examined esketamine's antidepressant mechanisms in chronic stress. After 21 days of stress and a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg), researchers measured hippocampal cannabinoid receptor (CB1R) and mitochondrial markers via Western blotting. Esketamine reversed stress-induced behavioral deficits and normalized CB1R-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis markers (NRF1, TFAM). CB1R antagonists blocked these effects, indicating CB1R signaling is essential for esketamine's rapid antidepressant response.

items.title: Reply to "Reading the Signal: What Psychedelic Trials in Depression Still Can't Tell Us".
items.summary_en: This is a reply article addressing methodological concerns raised about psychedelic trials in depression research. Without access to the full text, the specific counterarguments and evidence presented cannot be detailed, but such replies typically defend study design choices and data interpretation in clinical psychedelic research.

items.title: Q1 2026: Oregon Psilocybin Services Update
items.summary_en: Oregon Psilocybin Services released its first 2026 dataset covering Q1, providing insights into product sales, client motivations, and safety measures. The Psychedelic Alpha Tracker summarizes key data on service utilization and the organizations developing the OPS infrastructure.

items.title: Quality of life and productivity among esketamine responders in a real-world study in Australia and New Zealand.
items.summary_en: Real-world study of 84 treatment-resistant depression patients in Australia and New Zealand receiving esketamine nasal spray plus oral antidepressant for 16 weeks. 33% showed ≥50% symptom reduction. Responders demonstrated significant improvements: depression severity decreased 71%, quality of life increased 29.5%, and work productivity loss improved 35.9%. Mental health domain showed greatest quality of life gains.

items.title: Real-World Effectiveness and Cost-Differential of Intranasal Esketamine Versus Intramuscular Ketamine.
items.summary_en: Retrospective VA study (n=179) comparing intramuscular (IM) ketamine with intranasal (IN) esketamine for treatment-resistant depression. Both showed non-inferior efficacy (PHQ-9 difference: 0.04, 95% CI: -1.21–1.29) and comparable safety profiles. IM ketamine cost $647 per eight-treatment course versus $6,069 for IN esketamine, suggesting IM as a cost-effective alternative improving access to ketamine treatment.

items.title: Time-dependent effects of rapid-acting antidepressants in iPSC-derived neurons from treatment-resistant depression and healthy volunteers.
items.summary_en: iPSC-derived neurons from treatment-resistant depression patients and healthy controls were exposed to rapid-acting antidepressants including ketamine metabolite HNK, psilocybin, LSD, and DOI for 6-24 hours. RNA sequencing revealed that despite different mechanisms, all compounds converged on inflammation, mTORC1, and growth pathways. HNK showed distinct cell-type-specific effects in excitatory neurons, with results validated against ketamine-treated cerebrospinal fluid proteomics.

items.title: MDMA as an early post-trauma intervention in a translational animal model of PTSD.
items.summary_en: Controlled study in 175 rats examined MDMA's preventive potential for PTSD following predator scent stress. The 10 mg/kg dose, administered 30 minutes or 24 hours post-trauma, significantly reduced anxiety-like behavior, startle response, and contextual freezing. Effects correlated with increased corticosterone, hippocampal glucocorticoid receptor expression, and serotonergic markers. Lower doses and delayed administration without trauma-cue pairing were ineffective.

items.title: Targeting TLR4/PPARα-mediated neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex: S-ketamine and S-HNK rapidly alleviate depression-like behaviors.
items.summary_en: Mouse study investigating S-ketamine and S-HNK mechanisms in depression. Chronic social stress induced depression-like behaviors and neuroinflammation in the prefrontal cortex. Both compounds rapidly reversed behavioral deficits, restored neurotransmitter levels (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine), and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines by modulating TLR4/PPARα signaling.

items.title: Social hierarchy shapes behavioral and transcriptional responses to chronic stress and ketamine in male mice.
items.summary_en: Study in group-housed male mice using continuous behavioral tracking found that social hierarchy shapes stress responses. Dominant mice showed greater behavioral disruption under chronic stress, including fragmented rest and impaired social interactions. Single ketamine dose reversed these effects. mRNA sequencing identified 141 differentially expressed genes in the prefrontal cortex of treated dominant mice, suggesting hierarchy-dependent transcriptional mechanisms.

items.title: Real-world outcomes of intranasal esketamine and intravenous ketamine induction therapy for treatment-resistant depression in a community clinic: a retrospective cohort study.
items.summary_en: Retrospective cohort study (n=63) comparing intranasal esketamine (n=37) and IV ketamine (n=26) for treatment-resistant depression in a community clinic. Both groups showed similar baseline depression severity (PHQ-9 ~18) and comparable outcomes: mean PHQ-9 reduction ~10 points, response rates 65-69%, remission 23-32%, and clinically meaningful improvement 73-84%. Induction completion exceeded 90%. No significant differences between treatments.

items.title: Treating addiction with an addictive drug: the ketamine paradox revisited.
items.summary_en: A structured narrative review examined ketamine's potential for treating substance use disorders and treatment-resistant depression. Phase 2 trials show ketamine combined with psychotherapy reduces cravings and increases abstinence in alcohol and cocaine use disorders, but findings vary due to inconsistent dosing and follow-up protocols. While ketamine's glutamatergic mechanisms enable rapid neuroplasticity, concerns about abuse liability remain, requiring careful risk-benefit evaluation.

items.title: Rapid clinical and EEG microstate changes 24 h after intranasal esketamine in major depressive disorder with suicidal ideation: a prospective paired study.
items.summary_en: A prospective study of 31 hospitalized patients with major depression and suicidal ideation received intranasal esketamine alongside standard care. Clinical assessment and resting-state EEG were performed before treatment and 24 hours later. Depression scores improved significantly (HAMD-17: 25.3→20.6, n=22), while power spectral density remained unchanged. Microstate analysis revealed early alterations in microstate D occurrence and transition patterns, suggesting EEG microstates may be sensitive markers of rapid response to esketamine.

items.title: Intranasal esketamine plus oral antidepressant for treatment-resistant depression: acute induction and maintenance relapse-prevention outcomes in a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary_en: Meta-analysis of six RCTs (1,836 participants) comparing intranasal esketamine plus oral antidepressant versus placebo for treatment-resistant depression. Esketamine showed greater symptom reduction at day 28 (MADRS: -2.99) and faster improvement by day 2. Response and remission rates were significantly higher with esketamine. Maintenance phase data showed sustained benefit with lower relapse risk, though long-term safety requires further investigation.
items.notable_reason: Large meta-analysis synthesizing 6 unique RCTs (n=1,836) with both acute and maintenance phase data on esketamine efficacy and safety in TRD.

items.title: A ketamine/methionine exposure paradigm, alone or combined with Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, assessing schizophrenia-relevant behavioral, oxidative stress, and molecular endpoints in adult zebrafish.
items.summary_en: A ketamine/methionine exposure paradigm, alone or combined with Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, assessing schizophrenia-relevant behavioral, oxidative stress, and molecular endpoints in adult zebrafish.

items.title: Implementation factors shaping British Columbia's drug decriminalization pilot: A systematic review with narrative synthesis.
items.summary_en: British Columbia's 2023 drug decriminalization pilot, which removed criminal penalties for possession of 2.5 g or less of opioids, cocaine, methamphetamine, and MDMA, was terminated in January 2026. A systematic review of 27 peer-reviewed studies identified four implementation barriers: restrictive design features (low possession threshold, short timeframe), communication gaps between sectors, insufficient frontline training, and inadequate funding and infrastructure.
items.notable_reason: Systematic review of national-level drug policy implementation (decriminalization pilot) with 27 included studies, addressing harm reduction frameworks relevant to psychedelic regulation.

items.title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Abstract Screening and Evidence Mapping.
items.summary_en: Study benchmarks a local, open-source large language model pipeline for automating abstract screening in evidence synthesis. Using schema-constrained LLM architecture deployed locally (gpt-oss-20b via Ollama), researchers tested the system on three systematic reviews including ketamine/neuroimaging and clozapine studies. Results showed high performance: 100% recall and 98.9% F1 score for ketamine/neuroimaging; 79.3% recall for clozapine/suicidality. The local approach avoids proprietary cloud dependencies, improving reproducibility and scalability for biomedical literature synthesis.

items.title: Adolescent exposure to the psychedelic 25C-NBOMe in rats induces lasting competitive avoidance through disrupted hippocampal-prefrontal synchrony.
items.summary_en: Adolescent rats exposed repeatedly to 25C-NBOMe showed lasting competitive avoidance in adulthood, while adult exposure had no effect. Multisite recordings revealed disrupted theta synchrony between ventral hippocampus and orbitofrontal cortex. Chemogenetic manipulation of this pathway controlled the behavior, suggesting adolescent psychedelic exposure durably alters default mode network function and social behavior.
items.notable_reason: First-in-animal study demonstrating lasting social behavioral and circuit-level effects of adolescent psychedelic exposure with mechanistic pathway identified (vHPC→OFC synchrony).

items.title: Antidepressant-like effects of ketamine involve CX
items.summary_en: Ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist, produces rapid antidepressant effects through unclear mechanisms. This study investigates the role of connexin (CX) proteins in ketamine's antidepressant-like actions, advancing understanding of the molecular pathways underlying its therapeutic potential.

items.title: Ketamine-induced analgesia and dissociation show distinct behavioral and neural correlates.
items.summary_en: Within-subject fMRI study (n=37) comparing ketamine (0.4 mg/kg IV) to placebo found dissociable neural mechanisms for analgesia and dissociation. Ketamine produced both effects, but pain-related anterior insula activity and pain-predictive brain patterns were independent of dissociation intensity, which correlated instead with reduced default mode network connectivity. Results suggest ketamine's analgesic effects may not require dissociative experiences.

items.title: Emerging pharmacological and neuromodulation interventions for suicidal ideation and behaviour.
items.summary_en: A narrative review examined pharmacological and neuromodulation interventions for suicidal ideation and attempts. Analysis of 34 studies (22 pharmacological, 12 neuromodulation) found improvements within days to weeks in controlled trials. Promising results emerged for NMDA-related agents, opioid-system modulators, ayahuasca in treatment-resistant depression, and pimavanserin. SI improvements often exceeded concurrent depression changes, suggesting partial independence, though evidence remains inconsistent.

items.title: UK's regulatory and legislative double standards in the treatment of psychedelics and drugs for assisted suicide.
items.summary_en: This editorial examines regulatory inconsistencies in UK drug policy. Assisted suicide medications would circumvent standard approval processes despite limited evidence, while hallucinogens face substantial barriers despite promising international clinical data. The author argues assisted suicide drugs should undergo equivalent regulatory scrutiny, and hallucinogens should be rescheduled to facilitate further clinical research.

items.title: Clinical guidance on the use of esketamine nasal spray for patients with treatment resistant depression: A European Delphi consensus report.
items.summary_en: A modified Delphi consensus among 30 European psychiatrists established clinical guidance for esketamine nasal spray in treatment-resistant depression. Even modest symptom improvements during the acute phase (4-12 weeks) warrant continuation, particularly for patients with long disease duration and multiple failed treatments. Weekly 84 mg dosing was recommended to optimize outcomes. Monitoring should focus on residual symptoms, functional recovery, and comorbidities during continuation (6-9 months) and maintenance phases (≥12 months).

items.title: Case Report: Intranasal esketamine and accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation for severe treatment-resistant depression with suicidal ideation.
items.summary_en: Case report of a 29-year-old woman with treatment-resistant depression and suicidal ideation treated with intranasal esketamine combined with accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS). Ten iTBS sessions targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex were delivered over 4 days alongside esketamine (84 mg). Depression severity scores improved during acute treatment and remained stable at 2-week follow-up, with reported reduction in suicidal ideation.

items.title: DATAd: A new communication and tracking system for treatment-resistant depression.
items.summary_en: Researchers propose DATAd, a standardized tracking system for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Current staging models lack universal adoption, fragmenting treatment histories across providers. DATAd organizes trials into four categories: Drugs, Augmentation/combination, psychoTherapy, and Advanced treatments (TMS, ECT, ketamine). Clinicians document adequate and inadequate trials using simple notation, improving communication and identifying missed treatment opportunities.

items.title: Integrated 5-HT
items.summary_en: In vitro study using neural stem cell-derived models investigated how serotonergic psychedelics induce neuroplasticity. Testing tryptamines, phenethylamines, and ergolines alongside ketamine, researchers measured dendritogenesis, synaptogenesis, and BDNF expression. TrkB receptor activation proved essential for psychedelic-induced neuroplastic effects, suggesting a key mechanism linking acute effects to therapeutic potential.

items.title: Serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor following oral esketamine in treatment-resistant depression: Results from a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.summary_en: Randomized placebo-controlled trial examining serum BDNF levels in 54 treatment-resistant depression patients receiving six weeks of oral esketamine (90 mg/day) or placebo. While the primary depression outcome showed no group difference, BDNF increased similarly in both conditions during treatment and washout. BDNF changes did not correlate with depression severity changes in the esketamine group, questioning BDNF as a biomarker for oral esketamine response.

items.title: Ketamine use disorder: A case report.
items.summary_en: Case report documenting ketamine use disorder in a clinical patient. The study presents diagnostic criteria, clinical presentation, and treatment considerations for problematic ketamine use as a distinct substance use disorder, contributing to the clinical understanding of ketamine-related harms.

items.title: Psilocybin's effect on human brain synaptic plasticity.
items.summary_en: Single-dose psilocybin study (0.3 mg/kg, n=15) measured synaptic density changes via PET imaging in frontal cortex and hippocampus. No significant overall increase in synaptic markers was found. However, participants in therapeutic-like settings reported stronger mystical experiences and greater synaptic density increases than those in MRI scanners, suggesting environmental context modulates psilocybin's neuroplastic effects.

items.title: From Schedule I to the Clinic-Insights Into Psychedelic Drug Development From GHB.
items.summary_en: This viewpoint examines sodium oxybate (GHB) as a case study for how Schedule I substances, including psychedelics, can navigate regulatory pathways toward clinical approval. The analysis illustrates regulatory mechanisms that may apply to psychedelic drug development.

items.title: Micro-phenomenology of immersion and perceived presences under DMT.
items.summary_en: Study of 23 participants receiving 20 mg intravenous DMT with concurrent fMRI-EEG monitoring characterized immersion as a structured continuum using micro-phenomenological analysis. Detailed interviews identified 125 phenomenological categories across sensory, spatial, and social dimensions. Results show immersion develops hierarchically: bodily effects precede visual and auditory experiences, with perceived presences emerging only after multisensory integration and 3D spatial development.
items.notable_reason: First-in-human application of micro-phenomenology to DMT with simultaneous neuroimaging acquisition and detailed temporal analysis of immersive experience structure.

items.title: Ionic Homeostasis Failure in Major Depressive Disorder: Ion Channel Mechanisms, Excitation-Inhibition Imbalance, and Precision Therapeutics.
items.summary_en: A new framework proposes that major depressive disorder involves widespread failure of ionic homeostasis in neurons and glial cells. Genetic factors, chronic stress, and neuroinflammation disrupt calcium, potassium, and chloride balance, leading to excitation-inhibition imbalance and network instability. The review identifies key ion channels (CACNA1C, TREK-1, KCNQ, others) as therapeutic targets and discusses how ketamine, chloride-restoring drugs, and AI-guided approaches may enable precision treatments.

items.title: Backed by $11M NIDA Grant, Harvard Moves Forward on Ibogaine for Opioid Use Disorder Research
items.summary_en: Harvard receives an $11 million NIDA grant to advance multi-phase research on ibogaine for opioid use disorder treatment. The funding supports clinical development of this psychedelic compound as a potential therapeutic intervention, with additional support opportunities announced by ARPA-H.
items.notable_reason: Significant federal funding ($11M NIDA grant) for ibogaine clinical research at major institution, representing major policy/funding development in psychedelic medicine.

items.title: Acute Hallucinogen Intoxication Following Ingestion of a Commercially Available Mushroom Extract Product: A Case Report.
items.summary_en: Case report of an 18-year-old female presenting to emergency care with acute hallucinogenic intoxication after consuming a commercially available mushroom extract product. Clinical presentation included severe anxiety, agitation, visual and auditory hallucinations, paranoid ideation, and autonomic symptoms. Examination revealed tachycardia, tachypnea, dilated pupils, and psychomotor agitation. Diagnostic workup excluded co-ingestion and end-organ damage. The case highlights regulatory gaps in mushroom product labeling and potential psilocybin contamination in retail supplements.

items.title: Psychedelic therapy at the end of life: unexplored alternative to assisted suicide in the UK.
items.summary_en: Editorial examining psychedelic therapy as a potential alternative to assisted suicide in end-of-life care. Evidence suggests psychedelics reduce existential distress and suicidality in terminal patients. Author argues for rescheduling these substances to enable research on their role in palliative care before implementing assisted suicide policy in the UK.

items.title: Longitudinal dream-content shift and void-like dissociative phenomenology around outpatient ketamine infusions in chronic low back pain: a case report.
items.summary_en: Case report documenting dream content changes in a 48-year-old man with chronic low back pain over 16 years, including five low-dose ketamine infusions (15 mg) in 2014. Analysis of 50 masked dream narratives using a pre-specified coding scheme showed decreased obstruction motifs and increased social-interaction themes post-ketamine. Findings suggest possible links between ketamine's dissociative phenomenology and longer-term imaginal processes, without efficacy claims.

items.title: Combined DMT-harmine formulation reduces negative self-referential emotions during social self-evaluation: a randomized placebo-controlled trial in healthy volunteers.
items.summary_en: Randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial (N=28) examining combined DMT-harmine on self-referential emotions. Participants rated embarrassment and shame while listening to recordings of their own singing versus control vocals using visual analogue scales and the Experiential Shame Scale. HAR/DMT significantly reduced embarrassment compared to placebo in self-listening condition (p=.001), with no effect in control conditions. Harmine alone showed no significant effects.

items.title: Acceptability and safety of two sequential doses of psilocybin in bipolar II depression: protocol for an open-label single-arm feasibility study.
items.summary_en: Open-label feasibility study examining acceptability and safety of two sequential 25 mg psilocybin doses in 10 patients with bipolar II depression and suicidal ideation. Doses given 4 weeks apart with structured psychotherapy based on mindfulness cognitive-behavioural therapy. Addresses treatment gap in bipolar II, where standard pharmacotherapy often proves inadequate.

items.title: Enhancing plasticity to treat depression and other central nervous system diseases using event-driven pharmacology.
items.summary_en: Event-driven pharmacology proposes that plastogens—substances including ketamine and classical psychedelics—produce sustained neuroplastic effects from brief drug exposure, contrasting traditional occupancy-driven models. These compounds activate synaptic machinery and metaplasticity, potentially offering rapid-acting antidepressant benefits with fewer side effects than drugs requiring prolonged receptor occupancy.

items.title: Keeping Up with the Feds: From FDA to HRSA, Washington Backs Psychedelics
items.summary_en: US federal agencies including the FDA and HRSA are increasing support for psychedelic research and therapeutic development. This institutional backing signals growing recognition of hallucinogens' potential in clinical settings, reflecting a shift in regulatory approach toward these compounds.

items.title: FDA Issues Final Psychedelics Guidance, Schedules September Hearing on the Future of Psychedelic Therapies
items.summary_en: The FDA has issued final guidance on clinical investigations of psychedelics, building on a June 2023 draft document. The 11-page guidance covers nonclinical research, chemistry and manufacturing, clinical studies, and abuse potential assessments. After three years of stakeholder feedback, the FDA has scheduled a September hearing to discuss the future direction of psychedelic therapies.
items.notable_reason: FDA issues first formal guidance document on psychedelic clinical investigations, a national-level regulatory milestone affecting the entire field.

items.title: Changes in trauma symptoms of discrimination after MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder.
items.summary_en: A preliminary study (n=5) examined MDMA-assisted therapy for trauma symptoms related to discrimination using the Trauma Symptoms of Discrimination Scale. Paired t-test showed a 38% reduction in scores (p=.046, Cohen's d=1.28). All participants reported marked improvements across diverse racial/ethnic backgrounds and discrimination histories. Results suggest MDMA-assisted therapy may reduce discrimination-related trauma in marginalized populations, though larger studies are needed.

items.title: Brain-targeted epigenetic effects of two emerging psychoplastogens: ketamine & MDMA.
items.summary_en: Brain-targeted epigenetic study examined DNA methylation changes in 20 ketamine and 16 MDMA clinical trial participants. Both psychoplastogens altered 300+ genes each, with convergent effects on neuroplasticity and neuroimmune pathways. Blood and saliva samples analyzed pre/post-treatment using linear mixed-effects models reveal peripheral epigenetic mechanisms underlying therapeutic effects for mood and trauma disorders.

items.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy in treatment-resistant depression: rapid remission, uncertain durability, and the next phase of clinical evidence.
items.summary_en: Psilocybin-assisted therapy shows rapid symptom reduction in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but long-term durability remains unclear. Early randomized trials demonstrate promising short-term remission rates, yet evidence is limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and inadequate comparison with established TRD treatments like esketamine and electroconvulsive therapy. Key questions about sustained benefit and effects of repeated dosing remain unanswered.

items.title: Epigenetic landscapes of classical psychedelics and ketamine: molecular mechanisms of long-lasting neuromodulation.
items.summary_en: Review examining how classical psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT, mescaline) and ketamine produce lasting neuroplastic changes through epigenetic mechanisms. Evidence suggests therapeutic effects in neuropsychiatric conditions involve DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin restructuring, and non-coding RNA dynamics. Psychedelics modulate metabolic pathways affecting epigenetic cofactors, potentially driving persistent transcriptional changes and enhanced synaptic connectivity, though direct causal evidence remains limited.

items.title: Psychedelics and the thalamocortical system: A scoping review.
items.summary_en: A scoping review examined how psychedelics affect the thalamocortical system, synthesizing preclinical and clinical evidence using PRISMA methodology. The review focused on NMDA antagonists, serotonin 2A agonists, and iboga alkaloids. Psychedelics show therapeutic promise for depression, trauma, OCD, and substance use disorder. Since several psychiatric conditions—depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism—involve thalamocortical alterations, understanding thalamic function could advance psychedelic research and biological psychiatry.

items.title: Personality changes following first-time psychedelic use in college students in Germany.
items.summary_en: A one-year longitudinal study of 102 first-time psychedelic users and 1,066 controls among Berlin university students found small increases in Openness and decreases in Conscientiousness (Big Five Inventory), though effects were modest and attenuated after adjusting for confounders. Changes were not clearly distinct from other first-time illicit substance users. Participants with psychiatric diagnoses showed larger Neuroticism reductions. Causal interpretability remains limited.

items.title: Navigating 'k-land': a qualitative exploration of participants' experiences of ketamine-assisted psychotherapy for methamphetamine use disorder.
items.summary_en: Qualitative study of 14 participants in an open-label pilot trial examining experiences of ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) for methamphetamine use disorder. Semi-structured interviews identified four themes: prior limited treatment success prompting openness to novel approaches; importance of relational safety and clinical containment; reduced emotional reactivity following ketamine sessions; and translation of psychological shifts into behavioral change. Findings suggest KAP acceptability and potential mechanisms in this population.

items.title: Psychedelics in Mental Health: Opportunities and Challenges.
items.summary_en: A special issue examines psychedelics' potential in treating depression, PTSD, and substance disorders. While early trials show promise, key questions remain about mechanisms, safety, and ethics. Research emphasizes that psychedelic therapy involves more than pharmacology: therapeutic relationships, preparation, integration, and cultural context significantly influence outcomes. Subjective experience and meaning-making appear central to therapeutic change.

items.title: Convergent increases in serotonin 1B receptor binding following ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy: a multi-centre bayesian re-analysis of PET data.
items.summary_en: A multi-centre Bayesian re-analysis of PET imaging data found convergent increases in serotonin 1B receptor binding following both ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). The study used PET neuroimaging to measure in vivo serotonin 1B receptor availability, suggesting these two distinct antidepressant treatments may share a common neurobiological mechanism.
